newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares sprinted ahead to close at a new record and dealers foresaw more rises if the Federal Reserve policy makers leave U.S. interst rates unchanged after tonights' meeting.
The AEX share index rose 7.71 points to close at the highest level ever of 879.02. Dealers said the rising dollar supported the already positive undertone in the market.

Only few players cast some doubts about the outcome of today's FOMC-meeting. "It is difficult to predict what (U.S. Fed-chairman Alan) Greenspan is going to say tonight," said one dealer, adding he had provided the market with surprises before.
KLM caught the eye of investors after the firm said it was mulling the sale of its stake in U.S. carrier Northwest.
KLM shares rose almost six percent or 3.40 guilders to 63.70. Dealers said the market was expecting another move from KLM if the sale went ahead.
"The sell-off of the Northwest stake on its own is not the good news," said one dealer, adding Northwest made a strong contribution to KLM's 1996/97 earnings.
"They will make quite a bit of money if they sell their stake in Northwest, but it would also mean that Nortwest will not contribute to their annual earnings any longer," he said.
Dealers said it was important to know which partners would be available for KLM to form an alliance.
Some dealers believe that a link-up with British Airways is still possible.
"KLM shares will rise above 70 guilders if they find a good partner," said one dealer.
Another dealer said the Dutch share market would climb further if the U.S. dollar kept strong.
The dollar rose above 1.97 guilders in late afternoon versus 1.964 in early morning. International stocks rose strongly because of the rising dollar.
"Shares in Ahold, KLM, Unilever and Royal Dutch should benefit from the strong dollar," said one dealer.
